predecessors.name: Umayyad Caliphate
predecessors.text: Ifriqiya, whose governor Handhala ibn Safwan agreed in February 745 to return to Damascus rather than fight Ibn Habib

successors.name: Kharijite imamate of Ifriqiya
successors.text: Ifriqiya and Tripolitania, taken by the Warfajuma and Sufri Berbers (Kairouan, 757) and the Ibadites (Tripoli, 757)

ledger.x: 745: Abd al-Rahman ibn Habib takes Ifriqiya.
The page says only that the Ibadites revolted under al-Harith after Ilyas moved against them in 747, and that Tripolitania was reconquered in 752.
757: Kairouan falls and the dynasty ends.
757: the Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri 'recaptured Tripoli'.
757: the Fihrid emirate of Ifriqiya ends.

wars.name: Ibadite revolt in Tripolitania
wars.outcome: Ilyas ibn Habib moves against the Ibadites in 747; they rise under the imam al-Harith; in 752 an Ifriqiyan army reconquers Tripolitania and drives the remnants into the Jebel Nafusa.

wars.name: Kharijite conquest of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: The Warfajuma and Sufri Berbers take Kairouan and kill Habib (757); the Ibadites under Abu al-Khattab al-Ma'afiri retake Tripoli (757) and Kairouan (758), founding the imamate.

certainty.note: No frontier is named on the pages opened; the Maghrib frontier (eastern Algeria out of reach) and the Saharan edge are approximate.
